title: The SSD Filter
briefing: Floor 3: storage! SSDs arrive by the crate, and about a third of them are duds. Loops with append work, but this floor runs FAST. Head office wants the whole filtering job done in single lines using comprehensions. Show them what you've got.
hints: A list comprehension is [expression for item in list if condition]. For example: [s for s in ssds if s["health"] >= 20].
A dict comprehension uses {key: value for ...}. To flatten a list of lists, use two for parts: [x for row in shelves for x in row]. A lambda is a tiny function: lambda gb: gb / 1000.

working = [s for s in ssds if s["health"] >= 20] / serials = [s["serial"] for s in working] / to_tb = lambda gb: gb / 1000 / sizes_tb = [to_tb(s["gb"]) for s in working] / capacity = {s["serial"]: s["gb"] for s in working} / all_slots = [slot for row in shelves for slot in row]
bonus: Make a list of the squares of 1 to 10 in one line. Then make only the even squares.
